### CVE-2000-0380
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2000-07-12 | Updated: 2024-08-08 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 19882: Cisco IOS 11.x/12.x - HTTP %% (remote/hardware, 2000-04-26, verified=1)

The IOS HTTP service in Cisco routers and switches running IOS 11.1 through 12.1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service by requesting a URL that contains a %% string.

### CVE-2000-0613
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2000-10-13 | Updated: 2024-08-08 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 20067: PIX Firewall 2.7/3.x/4.x/5 - Forged TCP RST (remote/hardware, 2000-07-10, verified=1)

Cisco Secure PIX Firewall does not properly identify forged TCP Reset (RST) packets, which allows remote attackers to force the firewall to close legitimate connections.

### CVE-2000-0955
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2000-11-29 | Updated: 2024-08-08 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 20372: Cisco Virtual Central Office 4000 (VCO/4K) 5.1.3 - Remote Username / Password Retrieval (remote/hardware, 2000-10-26, verified=1)

Cisco Virtual Central Office 4000 (VCO/4K) uses weak encryption to store usernames and passwords in the SNMP MIB, which allows an attacker who knows the community name to crack the password and gain privileges.

### CVE-2000-1022
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2001-01-22 | Updated: 2024-08-08 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 20231: Cisco PIX Firewall 4.x/5.x - SMTP Content Filtering Evasion (remote/hardware, 2000-09-19, verified=1)

The mailguard feature in Cisco Secure PIX Firewall 5.2(2) and earlier does not properly restrict access to SMTP commands, which allows remote attackers to execute restricted commands by sending a DATA command before sending the restricted commands.

### CVE-2000-1027
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2001-01-22 | Updated: 2024-08-08 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 20369: Cisco PIX Firewall 5.2 - PASV Mode FTP Internal Address Disclosure (remote/hardware, 2000-10-03, verified=1)

Cisco Secure PIX Firewall 5.2(2) allows remote attackers to determine the real IP address of a target FTP server by flooding the server with PASV requests, which includes the real IP address in the response when passive mode is established.
